summary: Shoko Watanabe worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930) and under Ernst Leumann (~1930–1931), later holding posts at Kyushu University (~1947–1959), Toyo University (~1959–1977), and Taisho University.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Shoku Bando studied at Kyoto University of Education (~1968–1972), Otani University (~1972–1975), and the University of Freiburg (1984–1986). In 1987, he held posts at Abhidharma Kenkyūjo, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoren Ihara worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965 and 1977) and the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996 and 1998).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Shoryu Katsura studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto under Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held posts at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Shoshin Fukihara studied at Otani University (~1928–1931) and Horyu-ji, and under Join Saeki and Susumu Yamaguchi. His career included posts at Otani University, Doho University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, and Otani University Junior College (~1950–1973).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Shoshin Ichishima served as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaii. He held multiple posts at Taisho University, where he was attested as Dean of Academic Affairs in 1983 and Professor Emeritus in 2014.

Shoshin Kuwayama specialized in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University (~1957–1966) and served there as Assistant Professor (~1972–1988).

Shoson Miyamoto worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1928–1943), Komazawa University (~1954–1974), Waseda University (~1954–1969), and the Japanese Association of Indian and Buddhist Studies (~1951–1983).
Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of history, archaeology, and sinology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1984–2007) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2004–2006).

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Shoyu Hanayama studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1959). He served as a professor at Musashino University (~1969–1995) and as Chairperson of Bukkyō Dendō Kyōkai until 1995.

Shozen Kumoi worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Otani University (~1938–1941). He served at Otani University (1948–1981; emeritus ~1986–2017), Bukkyo University (1982), Kyoto University (1971–1973), and the University of Vienna.
Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology. He held posts as professor at both the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaii, attested in 2016.

Shridhar Ramkrishna Bhandarkar worked in Indology. In 1884, he served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute, later holding Sanskrit professorships at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, Mumbai.

Shrikant S. Bahulkar worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Vasudev Vishwanath Gokhale and held positions at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (attested 2000) and as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar worked in Indology and philosophy, having studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak. He served as General Secretary of the All-India Oriental Conference (~1919) and Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1929).
Shrivatsa Goswami specialized in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and held a post at the Vrindaban Research Institute, attested in 1994.

Shu-chen Chen studied Buddhist studies and philosophy at the University of Virginia (attested 2007) under doctoral supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen C. Lang. In 1996, Chen served as a teaching assistant at the University of Virginia.

A scholar of linguistics and Indology, Shu-fen Chen studied at National Tsing Hua University and completed a doctorate under Hans Henrich Hock. Chen served as a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shu-fen Liu specializes in Buddhist studies, sinology, history, and archaeology. Career posts include positions at Academia Sinica (attested 2012) and as Professor at its Institute of History and Philology (attested 2018).

Specializing in Indology, Shubhachandra held a post as Professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and an affiliation with the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).
